existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Proof note on the E8 line model behind the P104 caller, with a stated hypothesis ledger: a duality between isotropic transvection words and reflection words with product -I (Theorem G); a Gram-class floor c >= 56 for 16 to 24 deleted lines with the exact equality design (Theorem O); flattening of nested-frame chains onto the mask with a conditional transfer of the floor (Theorem F, Corollary F2); an A2 toy showing the naive transfer fails; the subspace frames as the geodesic interval of Lagrangian frames and a 1-Lipschitz retraction onto them (Theorems I and R, exhaustive for h <= 4); exact tile caps over all subspaces for one 104-line port set; and the Schur law and leak identity for owned lifetimes. No word is built and no kappa is claimed.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a joint helper basis and a legal causal split on the complete invoice. This package builds no word and prices no supplier; it states conditional structural results about the owned layer, the frame family and the root-word algebra, each with its hypotheses, and keeps every open door at a named hypothesis.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the statements constrain the owned-layer floor, the frame family and the helper-form algebra of any word in the stated model. They say nothing about the denominator or about kappa.
stop_rule: No kappa claim and no new word. Open and stated: the Gram-class floor for 25 or more and 15 or fewer deleted lines; carriers outside col(E); owned networks that are not flag chains (forks with later reads or writes, relays, owned ascent); the network reading of the retraction (two Clifford premises); geodesic tiles versus linear tiles; word-level membership in the flag-chain class.
evidence: README.md and THEOREM.md (statements, proofs, hypothesis ledger), check.py with checks/ (exact rational and integer certificates, standard library only) and data/ (quoted-line table, one 16-line pair system).

open_questions.question: Can the Gram-class floor of Theorem O be proved for 25 or more deleted lines, and for 15 or fewer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem O covers 16 to 24 deleted lines, which contains the P104 port set; other port sets need the same floor to compare gains.
open_questions.first_step: For 25 or more, count how many independent tops can have codimension at least 2 at once (joint star counts); for 15 or fewer, use the per-term level law with the end-line saving.
open_questions.blocked_by: Joint counts of high-codimension stars are not part of this package, and the argument for 15 or fewer needs biorthogonality that general invertible M does not give.

open_questions.question: Is a given word's owned layer a disjoint union of flag chains whose flattened terms form a Gram-class design?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Corollary F2 transfers the floor 56 only under that membership.
open_questions.first_step: Extract the owned chains of one shipped word, check nesting of frames, flatten, and compare the flattened terms with a Gram-class design up to a sign gauge.
open_questions.blocked_by: No word is replayed in this package.

open_questions.question: Do the floors survive owned networks that are not flag chains?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Forks with later reads or writes and relays can compute a rank-two object with shared trunk mass, so the rank-one cost model may overprice them.
open_questions.first_step: State the weakest network class for which Theorem F's read-before-write argument still gives a flattening, then test a fork instance exactly.
open_questions.blocked_by: Theorem F uses that levels are non-decreasing in time; ascent breaks it (control in section 3 of THEOREM.md).

open_questions.question: Does the retraction of Theorem R extend to helpers with non-family endpoints, and do geodesic tiles reduce to linear tiles?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The network reading of Theorem R and the tile caps only matter if no cheaper non-subspace frame or tile exists.
open_questions.first_step: Check helper step patterns with two or more family contact stops at h = 4 for a family replacement with the same steps, and prove the reduction of an additive-step tile to a linear tile.
open_questions.blocked_by: Exhaustive checks stop at h = 4, and the tile reduction needs the equality case of a rectangle bound on Hadamard matrices, not proved here.
